add.k: A pilot who commands the flying fortress Sky Harbor
st: In season 3, Baron Von Rantenraven attacks New York from Sky Harbor with old biplanes, until Spider-Man brings the fortress down.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). Wikipedia's synopsis says his capture is mentioned on screen ('Baron von Rantenraven and his men are in police custody'). Sky Harbor (S3 3a, Sky Harbor).

st: In season 2, Uncle Ben is murdered by a thief Peter let escape, which teaches Peter that great power brings great responsibility.

files.notes: Named as in the app's other Ben Parker files. Peter says 'Uncle Ben is dead' (episode quotation). Only on screen in The Origin of Spider-Man! (S2E1, show episode 21); S1 6b only mentions his grave. tm Independent, no group.

st: In season 1, Blackwell haunts his old theatre to save it from demolition, then helps Spider-Man beat the Green Goblin, who robs him.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). His name is shown on the theatre poster (Farewell Performance, S1 13b) and in the Magic Malice synopsis (S1 17b). His page also puts him in S1 6b, but the 6b episode page and Wikipedia call that magician Grandini the Mystic, so 6b is left out. The theatre (Castle Theatre / Old Castle Theatre) is not confirmed as his employer or by its on-screen name, so tm is Independent.

add.k: A safecracker who times his blasts to thunder
st: In season 2, Boomer flees Spider-Man after a bank blast, frees a Martian warrior to help him rob gold, and is caught by Spider-Man.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). The Martian is 'Bolton' in Wikipedia and 'Vulcan' on the Marvel Database, so he is left unnamed. Boomer also shows up in reused footage in Trip to Tomorrow (S3E13); no new story there, so no step. Thunder Rumble is S2E16 (show episode 36).

st: In season 1, Brutus guards Charles Cameo, knocks Spider-Man down and poses as a police officer, but Spider-Man catches him with Cameo.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). No character page; synopses of Double Identity (S1 19b) name him as Cameo's bodyguard. Not the dog Brutus of The Vanishing Doctor Vespasian.

add.k: An alien girl with spider powers
st: In season 2, Carol makes a date with Peter, who finds she is an alien stealing gear to save her people, until a ray takes them home.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). 'Carol' is the name she uses on Earth. Her people are called spider-men in the synopsis but no group name is confirmed, so tm is Independent. Home is S2E14 (show episode 34).

add.k: A former filmmaker with a Spirit-Scope
st: In season 2, Clive brings the monster Blotto to life with his Spirit-Scope to seize the city, until Spider-Man takes the Scope.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). Wikipedia says film producer, his page says director, so k says filmmaker. Arrested with his assistant Colin at the end (Wikipedia). Blotto is S2E15 (show episode 35).

add.k: An impresario the Fiddler tries to extort
st: In season 1, the Fiddler attacks Cyrus Flintridge III's band for a ransom; after Spider-Man wins, Flintridge knows him as Otto.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). Spelled Flintridge in both synopses (the page title has Flintrige). 'Impresario' follows the app's Fiddler file. His tie to the band is not clear enough to call it a group, so tm is Independent. Fiddler on the Loose is S1 18b.

add.k: A conquistador who rules the Cloud City of Gold
st: In season 2, DeVargas captures the crash survivors and fires a cannon at Spider-Man, setting off the volcano as they escape.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). No character page. His fate in the eruption is not stated, so Missing. Cloud City of Gold is S2E12 (show episode 32).

add.k: A cowboy thief on a flying robot horse
st: In season 3, Desperado robs banks with hypnotic guns from a flying robot horse, until Spider-Man uses Jameson as bait and webs him up.

files.notes: Named in the title card (Spider-Man vs. Desperado, S3 2b, show episode 41). No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page).

add.k: A diamond smuggler who hides diamonds in ice
st: In season 2, Doctor Cool locks Spider-Man in a deep freeze with stolen diamonds, until Spider-Man buries him and his henchman in ice.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). Wikipedia's Cold Storage synopsis (S2E18, show episode 38) names him and says he is captured.

add.k: A villain who enslaves people with robot bugs
st: In season 2, Dr. Manta enslaves people at his island castle with robot bugs, until Spider-Man answers a distress call and frees them.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). The synopses say he is defeated, not that he is captured or arrested, so the status is At large. Wikipedia says the slaves are the island's people, the Marvel Database says New Yorkers, so the step says people. Phantom from the Depths of Time is S2E8 (show episode 28).

st: In season 1, Doctor Smartyr calls off Spider-Man's fight with the Plutonians who seize him, then Doctor Octopus steals his Nullifier.

files.notes: No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page). On screen in Sub-Zero for Spidey (S1 1b) and The Terrible Triumph of Dr. Octopus (S1 17a). tm Independent.

add.k: A mad scientist with an invisibility serum
st: In season 3, Doctor Vespasian turns himself invisible to destroy Spider-Man and rob a bank, until Spider-Man drops ice cream on him.

files.notes: Named in the title card (The Vanishing Doctor Vespasian, S3 4a, show episode 43); Wikipedia synopsis used. Defeat is stated, no capture or arrest is, so the status is At large. No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page).

add.k: A scientist in a slippery, non-stick suit
st: In season 1, Doctor Von Schlick steals oil from a tanker in his slippery suit, until Spider-Man tracks him to his sewer base.

files.notes: Named in the title card (The Slippery Doctor Von Schlick, S1 15b). Defeat is stated, no capture or arrest is, so the status is At large. No transcripts exist for the 1967 show; the name rests on the episode synopses (Wikipedia episode list, Marvel Database episode page).

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Baron Von Rantenraven attacks New York with biplanes from Sky Harbor, and the Mayor calls in Spider-Man. Spider-Man tricks the pilots with a mirror and crashes the Baron's plane into a zeppelin holding up the fortress.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who brings down Sky Harbor
stages.whoB: The baron whose flying fortress he brings down

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Ben is Peter's uncle. Peter, newly given spider powers, lets a thief escape a TV station, and that thief later murders Ben. Peter catches him and vows to use his powers responsibly.
stages.whoA: His nephew, who let his killer escape
stages.whoB: His uncle, murdered by a thief Peter let go

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Ben is May's husband and Peter's uncle. He is murdered by a thief that Peter failed to stop.
stages.whoA: His wife, Peter's Aunt May
stages.whoB: Her husband, murdered by a thief

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Spider-Man finds that Blackwell is behind the strange events at his old theatre, then helps him make Jameson spare it. Later the Green Goblin raids Blackwell's house, and the two beat him together.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who helps save his theatre
stages.whoB: The magician who helps him beat the Goblin

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: The Green Goblin plots to steal Blackwell's magic secrets and uses tricks to rob the city. He chains Spider-Man at Blackwell's house, but Blackwell helps Spider-Man defeat him.
stages.whoA: The Goblin, who steals his magic secrets
stages.whoB: The magician whose secrets he steals

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Jameson backs tearing down Blackwell's old theatre. Blackwell and the theatre's performers, helped by Spider-Man, trick Jameson into changing his mind.
stages.whoA: The publisher who wants his theatre torn down
stages.whoB: The magician who tricks him into sparing the theatre

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Spider-Man interrupts Boomer's bank blast and chases him, but loses him when a Martian warrior lands. Boomer frees the Martian to rob gold, and Spider-Man captures him once the Martian is gone.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who catches him after a gold heist
stages.whoB: The safecracker he catches after a gold heist

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Brutus is Charles Cameo's bodyguard and helps him steal art. He knocks out the officer delivering a tapestry and takes his place while Cameo poses as Spider-Man. Both are caught.
stages.whoA: His boss, a master of disguise
stages.whoB: His bodyguard and partner in theft

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Brutus knocks Spider-Man down while guarding Charles Cameo. When the police set a trap with a tapestry, Spider-Man catches Brutus along with Cameo.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who catches him with Cameo
stages.whoB: Cameo's bodyguard, who knocks him down

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Peter meets Carol at a club and they set a date. As Spider-Man he stumbles on her robbery, sees her spider powers, learns she is an alien, and stops a proton test that would destroy her people before they go home.
stages.whoA: Peter, the boy she makes a date with on Earth
stages.whoB: The alien girl he helps get home

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Clive sets the monster Blotto on the city with his Spirit-Scope. Spider-Man finds him, takes the Scope after a fight and uses it to turn Blotto back into film.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who takes his Spirit-Scope
stages.whoB: The man who unleashes Blotto

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: The Fiddler attacks Flintridge's band with sonic waves and demands a ransom of $1,000,000, then $5,000,000. After Spider-Man beats him, Flintridge recognizes him as Otto.
stages.whoA: The violinist who tries to extort him, Otto
stages.whoB: The rich man he tries to extort

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Spider-Man protects Flintridge's band from the Fiddler's sonic attacks. He defeats the Fiddler before the second ransom is paid.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who stops the Fiddler
stages.whoB: The man the Fiddler tries to extort

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Spider-Man leads the crash survivors to the Cloud City of Gold, where DeVargas sends a golden eagle after him and captures the others. DeVargas fires a cannon at him in the volcano, but Spider-Man frees everyone.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who frees his captives
stages.whoB: The conquistador who rules the Cloud City

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Desperado robs banks from his flying robot horse with hypnotic guns. Spider-Man sets a trap using Jameson, gets him off his horse and webs him up.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who webs him up
stages.whoB: The cowboy thief on a flying horse

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Spider-Man uses Jameson to set a trap for Desperado. The trap works and Desperado ends up webbed.
stages.whoA: The publisher used as bait in his capture
stages.whoB: The cowboy thief he is used to trap

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Spider-Man tracks Doctor Cool to his hideout, but Cool knocks him out and locks him in a deep freeze with the diamonds. Spider-Man wakes and later buries Cool and his henchman under ice.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who buries him in ice
stages.whoB: The smuggler who freezes him

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: A slave on Dr. Manta's island sends a distress call that Spider-Man picks up. He fights the robot beetles and the Mountain Monster, then beats Manta and frees the people.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who frees his slaves
stages.whoB: The slaver of the island castle

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Spider-Man tries to rescue Doctor Smartyr from ice creatures, until Smartyr stops him: the Plutonians only want help home. Later Doctor Octopus steals his Nullifier, and Spider-Man tracks him down.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who comes to his rescue
stages.whoB: The scientist he tries to rescue

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Doctor Octopus steals Doctor Smartyr's new weapon, the Nullifier. Spider-Man tracks him with a spider-tracer and holds him for the police.
stages.whoA: The villain who steals his Nullifier
stages.whoB: The scientist whose Nullifier he steals

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Doctor Vespasian turns invisible to destroy Spider-Man and impress the city's criminals. Spider-Man beats his invisible dog, then exposes Vespasian at a bank with ice cream.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who exposes him with ice cream
stages.whoB: The invisible scientist out to destroy him

stages.title: Spider-Man (1967)
stages.text: Spider-Man loses Doctor Von Schlick in a fire, then finds him stealing oil from a tanker. He tracks him to his sewer base and beats him.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who tracks him to the sewers
stages.whoB: The slippery oil thief
